title: The Burnt Cover
premise: Lena Hartwell, a sleepless interpreter haunted by the 'incident' at a collapsed ceasefire, receives a calendar invitation from her dead handler, Marek, scheduling a meeting for tomorrow — and when she arrives, she is pulled into an active operation she was never meant to survive. The invitation leads to a hidden dossier proving the incident was staged by elements of three governments to justify a hardline summit; the assassin who carried it out, codenamed Vesper, is now hunting everyone who knows. Lena must ally with a disgraced delegation security officer and use her linguistic skills to smuggle the truth past three intelligence services before the summit convenes. In the end, Lena confronts Vesper in the summit's old archive wing, chooses truth over the loyalty Marek trained into her, and broadcasts the dossier — surviving, but exiled from the profession that defined her.
about_author: A. M. Dunmore is the pen name of a former conference interpreter turned novelist who spent a decade behind the glass of high-stakes diplomatic talks. They write thrillers about people whose job is to be invisible — and what happens when invisibility fails.

chapters.title: The Invitation
chapters.summary: Lena Hartwell, running on four hours' broken sleep since the incident, opens her inbox to find a meeting request from Marek Voss — her handler, dead eleven days. The location is a café near the delegation compound. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into compulsion; she goes despite every instinct screaming otherwise.

chapters.title: Café Meridian
chapters.summary: At the café, Lena finds no Marek — only a stranger watching her, and a locker key taped under the table. When she pockets it, the stranger leaves a note: 'You were next on his list.' POV: Lena. Emotional beat: paranoia igniting; the ordinary world tilts.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: The station locker holds a burner phone and half a burned document — the 'burnt cover' — referencing Operation GLASSHOUSE and the incident Lena interpreted through. A text arrives on the burner: coordinates, midnight. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: grief curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Midnight meeting with Daniel Reyes, disgraced delegation security officer whom Marek trusted. He reveals Marek suspected the incident was staged. Gunfire interrupts — someone else came for the phone. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: wary alliance forged under fire.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: The shooter escapes; Reyes identifies the method as Vesper's — the assassin who executed the incident's 'loose ends,' possibly including Marek. Lena realizes the invitation wasn't a trap set by enemies but a dead man's insurance policy. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: cold clarity replacing fear.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: Reyes maps the machinery: intelligence services of all three summit governments each hold a piece of GLASSHOUSE, each believing the others ran it. Lena's value: she interpreted the incident and can spot the doctored transcript. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: scale of the conspiracy sinking in.

chapters.title: The Transcript
chapters.summary: In a safehouse, Lena reconstructs the incident transcript from memory, finding a ninety-second gap where the official record says nothing happened — and she remembers interpreting words that were later erased. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: her memory, long a wound, becomes a weapon.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Lena returns to her apartment to pack and finds it searched — professionally, politely. A single fresh lily on the table: Vesper's signature. She understands she's being given a chance to walk away. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: terror braided with defiance.

chapters.title: The Second Service
chapters.summary: Reyes brokers contact with a mid-level officer of the second government who wants GLASSHOUSE buried differently than his superiors do. The meeting is a test; Lena passes by catching a deliberate mistranslation meant to trap them. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: cautious trust earned through competence.

chapters.title: What Marek Taught Me
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: Lena remembers her training under Marek — loyalty above truth, the interpreter's oath of neutrality — and how he broke his own rules to build the dossier. POV: Lena (memory). Emotional beat: love and betrayal inseparable; the theme made intimate.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: En route to the third capital, their train is stopped. Vesper boards, walks the carriages, and passes Lena without recognition — then kills the second service's courier two cars back. POV: alternating close-third. Emotional beat: proximity to death; luck as a thin membrane.

chapters.title: The Archive
chapters.summary: Following Marek's final clue, they reach a private archive holding the original incident recordings. They find them — and find the archive already catalogued for destruction tomorrow. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: triumph undercut by the ticking clock.

chapters.title: Borrowed Time
chapters.summary: They copy the recordings, but the archive's alarm protocol alerts all three services simultaneously. Now every government knows someone holds the originals. Reyes proposes the impossible: get the truth into the summit itself. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: commitment past the point of retreat.

chapters.title: The Third Government
chapters.summary: A desperate approach to a third-service analyst yields an unexpected ally — someone whose sibling died in the incident. But the price is the recordings, and trust here is a currency nobody honors. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: hope that costs something.

chapters.title: Betrayal, Anticipated
chapters.summary: The analyst sells them out — or appears to. Lena, anticipating it via Marek's tradecraft, had fed them a poisoned copy. The real recordings stay hidden. Vesper closes in on the safehouse. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: grim satisfaction shadowed by exhaustion.

chapters.title: Safehouse Falling
chapters.summary: Vesper takes the safehouse while they're out; inside, he leaves the analyst's body and a message: the summit convenes in forty-eight hours, and Marek's name will be posthumously branded a traitor unless Lena surrenders. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: rage — Marek's memory weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Summit City
chapters.summary: They infiltrate the summit perimeter using Lena's still-valid interpreter credentials — the one door no one thought to revoke. Inside, she hears delegates rehearsing the official narrative of the incident in three languages, all of it lies. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the interpreter reclaiming her voice.

chapters.title: Forty Minutes
chapters.summary: Reyes engineers a forty-minute window in the summit's secure comms relay. Lena must translate the dossier live into all three working languages, untraceable, while Vesper hunts the building. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: white-knuckle focus; her craft as resistance.

chapters.title: Glasshouse Shattered
chapters.summary: The broadcast lands: delegates receive the recordings mid-session. Chaos erupts; one government moves to scapegoat its own service chief, another denies everything, the third goes silent. Vesper's contract is voided mid-hunt. POV: Reyes. Emotional beat: vertiginous victory — truth loose and uncontrollable.

chapters.title: The Archive Wing
chapters.summary: Vesper, unpaid but unfinished, corners Lena in the old archive wing — not for money, but because Marek was the only target who ever saw his face. Their confrontation becomes a negotiation: his silence for hers about what Marek truly was. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: the climax as moral choice, not gunfight.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Revised
chapters.summary: Lena chooses truth over the loyalty Marek demanded: she tells Vesper everything, including that Marek pitied him, and lets him walk — trading vengeance for testimony. She gives her full account to the summit commission, ending her career. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: grief finally allowed; identity rebuilt on honesty.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Weeks later, in a small coastal town under a new professional name, Lena sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. A letter arrives — unsigned, containing a pressed lily and no threat. She burns it, calmly, and watches the cover catch. POV: Lena. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; peace chosen, not granted.
